group.passage: In his 2008 book Outliers, the writer Malcolm Gladwell made an idea famous: that about 10,000 hours of practice is what it takes to become an expert at almost anything. Two readers sent the following responses to a magazine that had asked whether the “10,000-hour rule” still holds up.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Response A
passage_parts.text: The rule is often laughed at these days, but the research behind it is sound; it is the popular version that went wrong. In 1993, the psychologist Anders Ericsson and his colleagues studied violin students at a music academy in West Berlin. By the age of 18, the students judged to be the best had practiced alone for about 7,410 hours, compared with 5,301 hours for the good students and 3,420 hours for those training to become music teachers. Ericsson never claimed that one number guaranteed success; he later estimated that winners of international piano competitions practice about 25,000 hours. What matters is not hours alone but deliberate practice: work designed by a skilled teacher, with a clear goal and immediate feedback on every attempt. When Ericsson reexamined the studies his critics had relied on, keeping only those that measured this kind of practice, it explained 29 percent of the differences in performance, and 61 percent once errors in measurement were taken into account. Talent may open the door, but practice decides how far you walk through it.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Response B
passage_parts.text: No one denies that practice helps. The trouble is the belief that it explains nearly everything. In 2014, a team led by Brooke Macnamara combined the results of 88 studies and found that deliberate practice explained 26 percent of the differences in performance in games, 21 percent in music, and 18 percent in sports, but only 4 percent in education and less than 1 percent in professions. In 2019, the same team repeated the famous violin study with 39 violinists. This time, the best players had not practiced significantly more than the good ones. If hours cannot separate the good from the great, something else must be at work, such as working memory or other abilities people are born with. Telling teenagers that enough practice guarantees success is not only inaccurate; it may also lead those who fall short to blame themselves.

questions.stem: On which point would the two writers most likely agree?

options.A: Deliberate practice explains most of the differences between top performers and others.
options.B: The popular rule gives too simple a picture of how experts develop.
options.C: The 1993 violin study should no longer be trusted by scientists.
options.D: Inborn ability matters more than hours of practice in every field.

questions.stem: According to Response A, about how much more time had the best students spent practicing alone than the future music teachers by the age of 18?
Why does the writer of Response B mention the 2019 study?

options.A: To show that the newer study confirmed the findings of the 1993 study.
options.B: To show that violinists practice more than people in most other fields.
options.C: To suggest that the figures reported in the 1993 study were simply made up.
options.D: To show that hours of practice did not separate the best from the good.

questions.stem: Which of the following is presented as an opinion rather than a fact?

options.A: Deliberate practice explained less than 1 percent of the differences in professions.
options.B: In the 1993 study, the future music teachers had practiced alone the least.
options.C: Practice matters more than talent in deciding how far a person goes.
options.D: The 2019 study found no significant practice gap between the best and good players.

1.explanation_zh: A 說研究本身沒問題，「出錯的是流行的版本」，艾瑞克森從沒說過某個時數就能保證成功；B 說問題在於「練習幾乎能解釋一切」這種信念，告訴青少年練夠了就保證成功是不正確的。兩人都認為大眾流傳的一萬小時法則，把一個人如何成為專家說得太簡單了。
evidence: The rule is often laughed at these days, but the research behind it is sound; it is the popular version that went wrong.
Ericsson never claimed that one number guaranteed success; he later estimated that winners of international piano competitions practice about 25,000 hours.
The trouble is the belief that it explains nearly everything.
Telling teenagers that enough practice guarantees success is not only inaccurate; it may also lead those who fall short to blame themselves.

option_notes_zh.A: 只有 A 的立場：A 引用重新分析的結果強調刻意練習的重要；B 引用的數字顯示練習在多數領域只解釋一小部分差異。
option_notes_zh.C: 與 A 的立場相反：A 一開頭就說這項研究本身是可靠的；B 也只說重做的研究有不同發現，沒有說不該再相信。
option_notes_zh.D: 兩人都沒有這樣說；B 只說「還有其他因素在作用」，也沒有說天賦在每個領域都比練習重要。

A: When Ericsson reexamined the studies his critics had relied on, keeping only those that measured this kind of practice, it explained 29 percent of the differences in performance, and 61 percent once errors in measurement were taken into account.

In 2014, a team led by Brooke Macnamara combined the results of 88 studies and found that deliberate practice explained 26 percent of the differences in performance in games, 21 percent in music, and 18 percent in sports, but only 4 percent in education and less than 1 percent in professions.
C: The rule is often laughed at these days, but the research behind it is sound; it is the popular version that went wrong.
D: If hours cannot separate the good from the great, something else must be at work, such as working memory or other abilities people are born with.

1.strategy_zh: 多文本題先各寫下兩篇的立場（A：研究可靠、重點是刻意練習；B：練習重要但不是一切），再找兩人都同意的部分；只屬於其中一篇的主張要刪掉。
hints: A 認為出錯的是研究本身，還是流行的版本？
B 反對的是「練習有幫助」，還是「練習能解釋一切」？
兩人對「練夠一萬小時就保證成功」這種說法的看法一樣嗎？

2.explanation_zh: A 說 18 歲時，最優秀的學生獨自練習約 7,410 小時，未來的音樂老師約 3,420 小時；7,410 − 3,420 ＝ 3,990，約 4,000 小時。
evidence: By the age of 18, the students judged to be the best had practiced alone for about 7,410 hours, compared with 5,301 hours for the good students and 3,420 hours for those training to become music teachers.

option_notes_zh.B: 比錯對象：約 2,100 小時（7,410 − 5,301）是最優秀與「優秀」學生的差距，不是與未來音樂老師的差距。
option_notes_zh.C: 把「優秀」學生的練習總時數（5,301 小時）當成差距。
option_notes_zh.D: 受流行說法影響：一萬小時是大眾印象中的數字，不是文中兩組學生的差距。

B: By the age of 18, the students judged to be the best had practiced alone for about 7,410 hours, compared with 5,301 hours for the good students and 3,420 hours for those training to become music teachers.
C: By the age of 18, the students judged to be the best had practiced alone for about 7,410 hours, compared with 5,301 hours for the good students and 3,420 hours for those training to become music teachers.
D: In his 2008 book Outliers, the writer Malcolm Gladwell made an idea famous: that about 10,000 hours of practice is what it takes to become an expert at almost anything.

2.strategy_zh: 數字換算題先圈出題目要比較的兩組（最優秀 vs. 未來的音樂老師），再做減法；小心同一句裡第三組的數字（優秀學生）。
hints: 題目比較的是哪兩組學生？
這兩組在 18 歲時各練習了多少小時？
兩個數字相減大約是多少？

3.explanation_zh: B 先說 2019 年重做了那項小提琴研究，接著說「這一次，最優秀的演奏者練習得並沒有比優秀的多」，再推論「如果時數分不出好與頂尖，一定有別的因素在作用」。提到這項研究，是為了說明練習時數無法區分最優秀和優秀的演奏者。
evidence: In 2019, the same team repeated the famous violin study with 39 violinists.
This time, the best players had not practiced significantly more than the good ones.
If hours cannot separate the good from the great, something else must be at work, such as working memory or other abilities people are born with.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：1993 年的研究中最優秀的學生練得比優秀的學生多（7,410 對 5,301 小時），2019 年重做時「這一次」兩組卻沒有明顯差別，B 正是用這個不同的結果來質疑練習的解釋力。
option_notes_zh.B: 文中沒有比較小提琴手與其他領域的人誰練得多；B 引用的百分比說的是練習能解釋多少差異。
option_notes_zh.C: 說得太過：B 只說重做的研究有不同結果，沒有說 1993 年的數字是捏造的。

A: This time, the best players had not practiced significantly more than the good ones.

By the age of 18, the students judged to be the best had practiced alone for about 7,410 hours, compared with 5,301 hours for the good students and 3,420 hours for those training to become music teachers.
C: This time, the best players had not practiced significantly more than the good ones.

3.strategy_zh: 引述目的題看作者引用之後「接著說了什麼」：B 在研究結果之後用 If hours cannot separate… 下結論，目的就在這個結論裡。
hints: 2019 年的研究發現最優秀和優秀的演奏者有什麼差別？
B 接著從這個發現推出什麼結論？
1993 年的研究中，最優秀和優秀的學生練習時數有差別嗎？2019 年呢？

4.explanation_zh: C 改寫的是 A 最後一句「天賦也許能開門，但練習決定你能走多遠」，這是作者的看法，無法用研究數據證明。其他三項都是研究的結果或數據：職業領域低於 1%、未來的音樂老師練習時數最少（3,420 小時）、2019 年的研究發現最優秀與優秀者的練習量沒有顯著差異。
evidence: Talent may open the door, but practice decides how far you walk through it.

option_notes_zh.A: 這是 2014 年整合分析的結果（事實），出自 B。
option_notes_zh.B: A 列出的時數顯示未來的音樂老師練習最少（3,420 小時），是研究數據。
option_notes_zh.D: 這是 2019 年研究的發現，B 以事實的方式陳述。

A: In 2014, a team led by Brooke Macnamara combined the results of 88 studies and found that deliberate practice explained 26 percent of the differences in performance in games, 21 percent in music, and 18 percent in sports, but only 4 percent in education and less than 1 percent in professions.
B: By the age of 18, the students judged to be the best had practiced alone for about 7,410 hours, compared with 5,301 hours for the good students and 3,420 hours for those training to become music teachers.
D: This time, the best players had not practiced significantly more than the good ones.

4.strategy_zh: 事實與意見：能用研究、數據查證的是事實；作者的評價、比喻、建議是意見。注意意見常用比喻（open the door）或 may、should 等字。
hints: 哪些選項可以用文中的研究數據查證？
A 的最後一句是研究結果，還是作者自己的看法？
比喻句 open the door 想表達什麼意見？

translation_zh.text:
作家麥爾坎・葛拉威爾在 2008 年的著作《異數》中，讓一個想法廣為人知：要在幾乎任何領域成為專家，大約需要一萬小時的練習。一本雜誌問讀者「一萬小時法則」是否仍然站得住腳，以下是兩位讀者的回應。
【回應 A】這個法則如今常被取笑，但它背後的研究是可靠的；出錯的是流行的版本。1993 年，心理學家安德斯・艾瑞克森和同事研究了西柏林一所音樂學院的小提琴學生。到了 18 歲，被評為最優秀的學生獨自練習了大約 7,410 小時，優秀的學生是 5,301 小時，而將來要當音樂老師的學生是 3,420 小時。艾瑞克森從未說過某個數字就能保證成功；他後來估計，國際鋼琴大賽的優勝者練習了大約 25,000 小時。重要的不是時數本身，而是刻意練習：由技巧純熟的老師設計、有明確目標、每次嘗試都能立即得到回饋的練習。艾瑞克森重新檢視批評者所依據的研究，只保留真正測量這種練習的研究後，發現練習能解釋 29% 的表現差異；把測量誤差考慮進去後，更達到 61%。天賦也許能為你開門，但練習決定你能往裡面走多遠。
【回應 B】沒有人否認練習有幫助。問題在於相信練習幾乎能解釋一切。2014 年，布魯克・麥克納馬拉帶領的團隊整合了 88 項研究的結果，發現刻意練習能解釋遊戲類 26%、音樂 21%、運動 18% 的表現差異，但在教育只有 4%，在職業領域不到 1%。2019 年，同一個團隊以 39 位小提琴手重做了那項著名的研究。這一次，最優秀的演奏者練習得並沒有明顯比優秀的演奏者多。如果時數分不出優秀和頂尖，一定有別的因素在作用，例如工作記憶，或其他與生俱來的能力。告訴青少年只要練得夠就保證成功，不但不正確，還可能讓沒達到目標的人責怪自己。

options: 有目標、有回饋的刻意練習

open_tasks.prompt: Fill in a comparison table for Response A and Response B: each writer’s position, one piece of evidence, and one reason. Then write one English sentence saying which response you find more convincing and why.
reference_answers: Response A: position—practice is the key, if it is deliberate; evidence—the best violinists had practiced about 7,410 hours by 18; reason—the popular rule misread the research. Response B: position—practice helps but is not everything; evidence—practice explained only 4 percent of the differences in education; reason—the best and good violinists practiced about the same. I find Response B more convincing because it uses results from many fields.

Response A argues that deliberate practice explains much of expert performance, while Response B argues that other abilities also matter. I find Response A more convincing because it explains that the right kind of practice, not just the hours, makes the difference.
